subject: Follow-up: storage, logging, and PII handling for Oakwood pilot
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@oakwoodhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — PII / retention items we discussed

Hi Stephanie / Sean,

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can move to a legal/security review:  

- Scope: pilot will send short clinical notes (de-identified where possible) and joining patient IDs for routing.
- Key asks: we need clarity on what is persisted from the request (prompt) and the response (model output), where data is stored geographically, and what default retention periods/logging controls Redwood provides.
- Specific questions security asked us to confirm:  
  1) Are raw prompt texts written to persistent storage? If yes, for how long and where?
  2) Are generated outputs logged/stored anywhere outside the customer environment?
  3) Do embeddings or vector indexes get retained by Redwood?
  4) We need a simple matrix showing options for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and retention defaults.

I've attached the spreadsheet they requested with column placeholders. Also looping in our security team (sec@oakwoodhealth.com) — they may add a few specific controls.

Next step for us: if you can confirm the default behaviors and a list of options (and attachments you can share like SOC2), we'll package for our legal/security review. Can you respond with a short, bulletized confirmation?

Thanks,
Maria
---
Maria Gonzalez
Product Manager, Clinical Integrations
Oakwood Health

Attachments: oakwood-data-retention-table.csv (spreadsheet template)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@oakwoodhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-19T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — PII / retention items we discussed

Hi Maria — great speaking with you and thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, bulletized answer you can share with Security / Legal. I've attached a short SOC2 summary as requested.

Quick answers (hosted API defaults unless we agree otherwise):

- Prompts (request payloads): not persisted to long-term storage by default for standard Hosted accounts. We buffer in memory for inference and short-lived caches, but persistent request logs are retained for 30 days for troubleshooting and abuse detection. Retention can be configured to 0 days (no persistence) under an enterprise privacy addendum or by running on Redwood Private.

- Model outputs (generation results): treated similarly to prompts — not stored in a model artifact by default. Output streaming is transient; we persist output logs for 30 days by default for Hosted to support billing, analytics, and quality monitoring. For Dedicated, retention is configurable by the customer; for Private, Redwood does not retain copies by default (customer-managed).

- Embeddings & vector indexes: embeddings produced via our embeddings endpoint are stored only if you opt into the Redwood-managed vector store. For Hosted, if you use the managed store, vectors are stored in the US region by default and retained per customer policy (30 days default). If you do not use our managed store (recommended for sensitive pilots), embeddings are returned to you and not kept by Redwood.

- KV cache / session state: KV caches are ephemeral and tied to active GPU instances; they are not written to persistent storage.

- Data residency: Hosted (default) stores operational artifacts in US regions for customers registered in the US. Dedicated can be provisioned in specific cloud regions; Private deployments run in your VPC/on-prem and follow your residency controls.

- Audit logs & security evidence: We provide audit logs and can push them to your SIEM (S3/CloudWatch) for longer retention if required.

Next steps / options: 
1) We can produce a one-page matrix (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) showing defaults and configurable retention windows — will attach by end of day tomorrow.
2) Schedule a technical security call with our security engineer (Sean) and your sec team to walk through the controls — available Wednesday/Thursday.
3) If you need contract-level language (privacy addendum), we can share draft clauses.

Hope this helps — happy to tighten the language for legal.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-summary.pdf

On Jul 19, 2027, at 09:05, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Maria — great speaking with you and thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, bulletized answer you can share with Security / Legal. I've attached a short SOC2 summary as requested.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Oakwood Security <sec@oakwoodhealth.com>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@oakwoodhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up — embeddings storage

Alex / Maria — answering Alex's questions directly:  

- Vector store isolation: yes — our managed vector store is multi-tenant at the service layer but logically isolated per customer. Each customer has a separate namespace and access control.

- Encryption: data at rest is encrypted by default. We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private; Hosted can be configured to use CMK under enterprise agreements.

- Retention: you can choose not to persist vectors in our managed store (retention = 0) and instead receive embeddings back and index them in your own store. If you use Redwood-managed storage, retention is configurable — default 30 days for Hosted; Dedicated can choose retention windows, and Private leaves storage to you entirely.

Commitments for the pilot (what Redwood will (by default) do for Oakwood pilot):
- Prompts persisted: 30 days (Hosted default) unless we sign an addendum or you run Private.
- Outputs persisted: 30 days (Hosted default).
- Embeddings: not stored unless explicitly enabled; we recommend self-hosting vectors for pilot.
- Residency: US East for the pilot (we'll pin region in provisioning).
- Audit logs: we will export audit logs to your S3 bucket for the pilot (S3 link / permissions to be arranged).

Action items:
1) Stephanie: send matrix comparing Hosted/Dedicated/Private retention behavior (ETA: 2027-07-23).
2) Sean: schedule 60-minute security deep-dive with Oakwood sec (target: 2027-07-28).
3) Oakwood: provide S3 bucket details and preferred KMS config if you want audit logs pushed.

If that looks good, I'll prepare a short email you can forward to Legal that captures these pilot commitments.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
